### 1. Resolve revisions against a bare repository (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2.1, REQ-2.2, REQ-2.3, REQ-2.4

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the revision behaviours to internal/gitrepo/read_test.go (against a repository made with `git init` in t.TempDir()) and to internal/scm/revision_test.go (through a small test route) and confirm they fail
- 1.2 In internal/gitrepo, add the read primitives this package builds on, each taking a context and running the `git` binary through the package's runner: resolve a full ref name to a commit id with annotated tags peeled, list refs by prefix with ids, resolve a full or abbreviated commit id reporting 'not found', 'ambiguous' and 'not a commit' as distinct errors, and read an object's type and size
- 1.3 Never pass a caller's string to git as an argument that git could read as an option or as a revision expression: validate it first and give ids and ref names only in the forms the primitives define
- 1.4 In internal/scm, add the revision resolver with this order: a string starting with `refs/` is a full ref name and nothing else; otherwise look for branch `refs/heads/<s>` and tag `refs/tags/<s>` in the workspace's ref view, where both existing is ambiguous and one existing wins; otherwise accept 4 to 40 hexadecimal characters as a commit id; anything else is not a revision
- 1.5 Take the list of refs from the interface RefView declared in internal/scm so that a fork's view can be supplied later; the default view is the repository's own refs. Packages 21 and 22 resolve every revision through this one resolver and never through git directly
- 1.6 Answer every failure of resolution (unknown, ambiguous, not a commit, not one of the accepted forms) as the API error `ref_not_found` with status 404, built with the specific-type constructor of internal/server
- 1.7 Resolve an absent optional `ref` to the head of the workspace's default branch, read from the workspace record
- 1.8 Return a resolved revision as a value holding the full 40-character commit id and whether the caller wrote it as a full id, which the caching task reads later
- 1.9 Serve a commit by full id whether or not any ref reaches it, as long as the object exists

### 5. Serve one file, raw and as JSON, from one resolved commit (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-6.4, REQ-6.5, REQ-6.6, REQ-6.7, REQ-6.8, REQ-2.5

**Depends on:** 4

**Steps:**

- 5.1 Add the file behaviours to internal/scm/file_test.go and the concurrent-move behaviour to internal/scm/consistency_test.go and confirm they fail
- 5.2 In internal/gitrepo, add the blob read: look up a path at a commit and return its mode, blob id, type and size, then stream the blob's bytes
- 5.3 Implement the raw form of `GET …/scm/file`: check the size against the limit before reading content, then answer the bytes with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, `Content-Length`, `X-Parley-Blob-Sha`, `X-Parley-Resolved-Sha` and `X-Parley-File-Mode`; a symlink's content is its target
- 5.4 Honour a `Range` header that holds exactly one range: `a-b`, `a-` and `-n`, with an end past the file cut to the last byte, answered 206 with `Content-Range`; a start at or after the end is 416 with the new specific type `range_not_satisfiable` and `Content-Range: bytes */<size>`; several ranges are ignored and the whole file is answered
- 5.5 Implement the JSON form when `Accept` names `application/json`: `{path, sha, mode, size, encoding, content, resolved_sha}` with `utf8` for valid UTF-8 and `base64` otherwise; ignore `Range` in this form
- 5.6 Refuse a file larger than the configured limit with 413 `payload_too_large` and the member `size` in the envelope, in both forms and for ranged requests; a file of exactly the limit is served. Take the limit from a field of the route group that defaults to 32 MiB
- 5.7 Refuse a missing `path`, a directory, a submodule entry and an illegal path with 400 `invalid_request`, and a path that does not exist with 404 `path_not_found`; errors are the JSON envelope in both forms
- 5.8 Check, and where needed change, every route written so far so that each revision is resolved once at the start of the request and nothing later in the request reads a ref again; the concurrent-move test must pass for the file and the tree route

### 6. Serve the diff between two revisions (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-7.1, REQ-7.2, REQ-7.3, REQ-7.4, REQ-7.5

**Depends on:** 3

**Steps:**

- 6.1 Add the diff behaviours to internal/gitrepo/difftree_test.go and internal/scm/diff_test.go and confirm they fail; build the 5,001-file and the 3 x 3 MiB fixtures with `git fast-import`
- 6.2 In internal/gitrepo, add: the merge base of two commits (none is a result, not an error); the file changes between two trees with rename and copy detection on, giving path, old path, status, blob ids, line counts and the binary flag; and the unified patch of the same comparison with a chosen number of context lines, readable file by file
- 6.3 Build the file change object in one place in internal/scm, used by the diff, compare and commit routes: the six statuses, `old_path` only for renames and copies, null ids on the missing side, zero counts for binary files
- 6.4 Implement `GET …/scm/diff` in JSON: left side is the merge base in `merge_base` mode (the empty tree when there is none) and `base` in `direct` mode; answer `base_sha`, `head_sha`, `merge_base_sha` (null when there is none), `files` ordered by path, `stats` over the whole filtered diff and `truncated`
- 6.5 Apply the `path` globs with the matching rules of PLAT-FR-057 (`*` within a segment, `**` across segments, whole path, case-sensitive); a file matches when any glob matches; filtered-out files count nowhere
- 6.6 Honour `patches=false` (no `patch` members), `context` (default 3, 0 to 20) and `format=patch` (`text/x-diff` body)
- 6.7 Cut the result: at most 5,000 files; add patch text file by file until the next patch would pass 8 MiB in total and leave later files without `patch`; set `truncated` when either cut happened; in the patch format end the text at a file boundary and set `X-Parley-Truncated: true`
- 6.8 Refuse a missing `base` or `head`, an unknown `mode` or `format`, a `context` outside 0 to 20 and a non-boolean `patches` with 400 `invalid_request`
- 6.9 Extend the commit route's `files=true` from the commits task to use the shared file change object if it does not already

### 7. Compare two revisions with a trial rebase (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-7.5, REQ-7.6, REQ-7.7, REQ-7.8

**Steps:**

- 7.1 Add the compare behaviours to internal/gitrepo/trial_test.go and internal/scm/compare_test.go and confirm they fail, with one fixture branch per conflict kind
- 7.2 In internal/gitrepo, add the ahead and behind counts of two commits and the list of commits in one and not in the other, oldest first, with a cap
- 7.3 In internal/gitrepo, add the trial rebase: replay the commits of head that are not in base, oldest first, on top of base, entirely in the object store with no work tree, no index of the repository and no ref update (git 2.38's `merge-tree --write-tree` with an explicit merge base does one step); stop at the first commit that does not apply
- 7.4 Declare the one conflict report type of the hub, ConflictReport, in internal/gitrepo/conflictreport.go: target_sha, head_sha, base_sha, commit_sha, files (each path, kind, base, ours, theirs as {sha, mode, path} or null, and landed_by), landed_changes and change, encoded with every member present. Return from the trial either 'clean' or a ConflictReport with the commit that did not apply and, per conflicted path, the kind (`content`, `add_add`, `modify_delete`, `delete_modify`, and `rename`, `mode`, `binary`, `submodule` where git reports them) and the three sides, null where the file does not exist on that side
- 7.5 Report a merge commit among the commits to replay as a distinct error before replaying anything
- 7.6 Implement `GET …/scm/compare`: both revisions required (400 `invalid_request` otherwise); answer the ids, `merge_base_sha`, `ahead`, `behind`, up to 200 commit objects without stats, up to 5,000 file changes from the merge base to head without patch text, `mergeable` and `conflict`
- 7.7 Answer the trial's ConflictReport with `target_sha` = base, `head_sha`, `base_sha` = merge base, `commit_sha`, `files` with `landed_by: []`, `landed_changes: []` and `change: null`; packages 21, 23 and 24 return this same type from the rebase, the mergeability check and the restack, and package 26 fills the three members left empty here by extending this type, not by declaring another
- 7.8 Answer a merge commit in the range with 400 and the specific type `merge_commits_unsupported`; a head contained in base is `clean` with empty lists
- 7.9 Assert in the tests that the output of `git for-each-ref` is identical before and after every compare

### 10. Answer reads with caching headers and conditional requests (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-3.1, REQ-3.2, REQ-3.3

**Depends on:** 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9

**Steps:**

- 10.1 Add the caching behaviours to internal/scm/cache_test.go as tables over all ten routes and confirm they fail
- 10.2 Compute an `ETag` for every successful read as a quoted digest of: the resolved commit ids of the request, the route, the query string, and the representation (raw or JSON on the file route, JSON or patch on the diff route); for the two refs routes use the names and commit ids of the refs in the response instead of resolved ids
- 10.3 Set `Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable` when the route has revision parameters and the caller wrote every one of them as a 40-character commit id; an omitted optional `ref` is not a full id; the refs routes are never immutable
- 10.4 Set `Cache-Control: private, no-cache` on every other successful read, replacing the `no-store` default of the shared header middleware for these routes only
- 10.5 Add `Vary: Accept` on the file route
- 10.6 Answer 304 with no body and the same `ETag` and `Cache-Control` when `If-None-Match` contains the tag, alone or in a comma-separated list; decide this after resolution and before the expensive part of the read, so that a matching request runs no diff, blame or search
- 10.7 Leave error responses without `ETag` and with the shared default `Cache-Control`

### 12. Add the read commands of `parley scm` (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-10

**Depends on:** 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9

**Steps:**

- 12.1 Add the command behaviours to internal/cli/scm_test.go as tables that run the root command against an httptest server recording each request, and confirm they fail

- 12.3 Build each request with the HTTP client of the CLI foundation: the slug and, for `show`, the revision are percent-encoded as one path segment; a flag that was not given sends no query parameter; boolean flags send `true`; repeatable `--path` flags send one `path` value each; `--ignore-case` sends `case_sensitive=false`; `--lines <start>:<end>` sends `start_line` and `end_line`
- 12.4 Print the response body as the foundation prints every JSON result for `refs`, `log`, `show`, `ls`, `blame`, `search`, `compare` and `diff` without `--patch`; `ls` and `search` print the page the hub answered and do not follow `next_cursor`
- 12.5 `cat`: request the raw form; on success write the bytes unchanged to stdout, or with `--output` to that file, creating or replacing it only after the hub answered 200; on a hub error write nothing and leave an existing file as it was; a file that cannot be written is a `client_error`
- 12.6 `diff`: `--patch` sends `format=patch` and prints the text as received; `--name-only` sends `patches=false`; both together and a `--mode` other than `merge_base` or `direct` are usage errors
- 12.7 `compare --fail-on-conflict`: print the response, then when `mergeable` is `conflict` report `condition_not_met` through the foundation and exit 3
- 12.8 Register the group in cmd/parley so that `parley scm` without a subcommand prints help and exits 0
